summary: This program defines a RobotPet class whose battery level is guarded by a property, so any value assigned to it is automatically clamped into the range 0 to 100. Three pets are created and their details printed.

lines.text: Starts the blueprint for a robot pet; every pet created from it will share these attributes and methods.

lines.code: self.battery = battery  # uses the property setter for validation
lines.text: Assigning to self.battery inside __init__ does not create a plain attribute here; because a property named battery exists, Python routes this through the setter so even the starting value gets validated.
Marks the method below as the getter for an attribute called battery, letting readers write pet.battery without parentheses.
The getter simply hands back the hidden value stored in _battery.
Registers the next method as the code that runs whenever anything assigns to .battery, which is where the protection happens.
Receives the value someone tried to store so it can be checked before being saved.
Catches negative charge levels, which are physically meaningless for a battery.
Clamps anything below zero to the lowest legal reading rather than raising an error.
Catches attempts to overcharge past a full battery.
Stores 100 as the maximum, so the pet can never claim more than a full charge.
A value inside the valid range is stored as-is; the leading underscore signals that _battery is internal and should be reached through the property.
A behaviour that uses the battery level to answer a practical question about the pet.
Converts a walk length in minutes into the battery percentage it would consume.
Returns True or False by comparing the available charge with what the walk needs; note it reads self.battery, going through the getter.
Creates the first pet, passing name, battery, and mood into __init__.
An f-string builds a readable summary line; pet1.battery quietly calls the getter method.
